mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This mechanism operates continuously without requiring a specific threshold condition, as the rate level directly influences the cost of capital for corporations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.3 percentage points over a 3-month window signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes corporate earnings contraction and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous expansion in both the labor market (PAYEMS) and housing sector (HOUST) signals broad-based economic strength, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. The interaction effect is stronger than the sum of individual effects because both sectors are leading indicators of consumer spending and corporate investment.
failure_condition: The interaction term between PAYEMS and HOUST in a regression of 20-day SPX returns is not significant (p>0.05), or the Rank IC for the interaction signal falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In early expansion regimes characterized by accelerating industrial production (INDPRO growth > 2.0% YoY), the S&P 500 exhibits positive 60-day forward returns due to robust manufacturing output supporting corporate earnings growth and investor confidence in sustainable economic momentum.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of early expansion periods (defined by INDPRO growth > 2.0% YoY), or the Rank IC for INDPRO in early expansion regimes falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in retail sales (RSAFS) below 500,000 million dollars signals weakening consumer demand, which typically precedes a contraction in corporate revenues and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when RSAFS falls below 500,000, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), the S&P 500 tends to exhibit negative 60-day forward returns as higher borrowing costs pressure corporate margins and reduce equity valuation multiples. This mechanism is most pronounced in the mid-to-late stages of a rate-hiking cycle.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The industrial production index (INDPRO) exhibits a positive linear relationship with S&P 500 5-day forward returns, such that each 1-point increase in INDPRO predicts a 0.2% increase in SPX returns, reflecting the direct link between manufacturing output and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: The Rank IC between INDPRO and 5-day SPX returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation is not significantly positive (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1100.0 thousand units signals weakening residential construction activity, which typically precedes a slowdown in consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when HOUST falls below 1100.0, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.
